h: Canals, rock gardens and the little half-timbered lab
p: One of the most photographed views at Wisley is the long, formal canal stretching in front of the Laboratory, a handsome half-timbered building that looks far older than it is. It dates from the early 20th century and has long been a symbol of the garden, and it's a lovely spot to pause and take in the reflections on a still day.

The rock garden on the slope is another favourite, with alpine plants squeezed into nooks and crannies and little streams trickling between the stones. Further out, the woodland areas, the fruit fields and the model gardens give you plenty of ideas you can actually take home, whatever size your plot.

Seasonal events keep things fresh. A flower show usually takes over in late summer, and in winter the garden often hosts an evening light trail that turns the borders and trees into a glowing wonderland. Details and dates change from year to year, so keep an eye on what's planned.

Give yourself at least half a day, longer if you'd like to see most of it. The plant centre and shop are dangerous for your wallet if you're a keen gardener. When you're done, head into Woking itself, where a giant Martian tripod sculpture in the town centre celebrates H. G. Wells, who wrote The War of the Worlds while living in the town. The Lightbox gallery and museum by the canal is also worth a visit.
